Public Goods and Free-Riding

Everyone uses the same public good, but who pays to provide it? Public-good demands add up vertically, not horizontally.

Everyone consumes the same unit at the same time. So willingness to pay is stacked vertically. Where that sum meets the cost is the optimum. But each person reasons differently. Hoping others will pay, each pays nothing. Too little is collected, so supply falls short.

For example, 30 🧑 classmates chip in to buy a ⚽ ball for the classroom. The ball costs 30,000 won. If half think 'the others will pay' and pay nothing, the money falls short. Nobody gets a ball to play with.
